title: regextable
text: regextable extracts regex-based pattern matches data frame character vector using pattern lookup table, returning matched pattern, exact text match, internal row identifier, original columns input data unless specified, optional additional columns pattern table. text: demonstration, use two included datasets: members: lookup table regex patterns member names. cr2007_03_01: sample text dataset search.

title: regextable
text: extract() cleans text default, user need call manually. Cleaning standardizes spacing, punctuation, capitalization, helps regex pattern matching. Example clean_text():

title: regextable
text: simplest use extract(): Explanation: - data: text dataset search. - col_name: column contains text. - regex_table: lookup table patterns. - return_cols: columns data include result. - regex_return_cols: additional columns pattern table attach. row output corresponds detected match, includes original text matching pattern. —
code: result <- extract(   data = cr2007_03_01,   regex_table = members,   return_cols = c("text"),   regex_return_cols = c("icpsr") )  kable(head(result))

title: regextable
text: extract() can also filter data date, remove acronyms (-uppercase patterns 2+ characters), select specific output columns. useful controlled extraction. Explanation: - date_col, date_start, date_end: filter rows date. - remove_acronyms: skip patterns like “NASA” “USA”. can combine filters subset columns flexible outputs. —

title: regextable
text: Internally, extract() processes row text regex patterns order: Start text rows. Check regex pattern unmatched rows. match found, remove row checks. Continue patterns applied. approach improves performance large datasets rows stop checked match found.

title: regextable
text: regextable tool extracting data text. Use included datasets get started supply lookup tables. extract() default handles text cleaning efficient matching. Optional parameters allow advanced control filtering output.

title: Pattern-Based Text Extraction and Standardization with Lookup Tables
text: matching, default, clean_text() applied standardize text. lowercases text, removes excess punctuation, replaces line breaks dashes spaces, collapses multiple spaces single space. Text cleaning applied matching modify original input data. Users can disable behavior setting do_clean_text = FALSE.
code: text <- "  HELLO---WORLD  " cleaned_text <- clean_text(text) print(cleaned_text) #> [1] "hello world"

title: Extract pattern matches from text — extract
code: # Create sample data data <- data.frame(   id = 1:3,   text = c("I love apples", "Bananas are great", "Oranges and apples"),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE )  # Create regex patterns patterns <- data.frame(   pattern = c("apples", "bananas", "oranges"),   category = c("fruit", "fruit", "fruit") )  # Extract matches extract(data, "text", patterns) #> Matching 3 patterns against 3 text entries #>    |                                                  | 0 % ~calculating     |+++++++++++++++++                                 | 33% ~00s             |++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++                | 67% ~00s             |++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++| 100% elapsed=00s   #> Number of matches found: 3 #> # A tibble: 3 × 5 #>      id text               pattern match   row_id #>   <int> <chr>              <chr>   <chr>    <int> #> 1     1 I love apples      apples  apples       1 #> 2     2 Bananas are great  bananas bananas      2 #> 3     3 Oranges and apples apples  apples       3
